answer: A stake-weighted reputation market works like a reef: each agent must lock a refundable deposit before offering services, so a Sybil swarm pays the same bond per fake identity and earns nothing when its work is judged poor. Reviews are weighted by the reviewer's own earned history, not raw account count, so a sable-coated flood of fresh sock-puppets cannot outvote a few cedar-solid veterans whose stakes and track records are on the line. Attackers lose bonds and time, while honest agents keep compounding trust.
